The statement signals a highly accommodative, history‑dependent strategy: keeping the funds rate at 0–0.25% and continuing large Treasury/MBS purchases while aiming for inflation “moderately above 2 percent … so that inflation averages 2 percent.” In New Keynesian models and Taylor‑rule style analyses (Clarida‑Gali‑Gertler; Taylor), such a stance is appropriate when slack is present and inflation has run below target, with forward guidance and balance‑sheet policy substituting for further rate cuts at the lower bound. The average/forecast‑targeting flavor (Svensson; Woodford) helps anchor expectations and counteract the classic Barro‑Gordon inflation‑bias problem by making policy history‑dependent. The asset‑purchase program supports credit and lowers long rates/term premia via the yield‑curve channel, consistent with the literature on the Fed’s influence on long‑term rates and the broad credit channel (Bernanke‑Blinder). While describing the inflation pickup as “transitory” aligns with sticky‑price and cost‑push shock frameworks, real‑time mismeasurement risks (Orphanides) and virus uncertainty temper the outlook. Net tone: cautiously optimistic given strengthening activity/employment and accommodative financial conditions, but balanced by residual risks.
